subject: math
title: Natural Numbers and Fractions
summary: Understanding natural numbers, factors, multiples, and introduction to fractions

sections.title: Natural Numbers
sections.content: Natural numbers are counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ... They are used for counting objects. The smallest natural number is 1. There is no largest natural number because they go on infinitely. Natural numbers can be represented on a number line.

sections.title: Factors and Multiples
sections.content: A factor of a number divides it exactly without leaving a remainder. For example, factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. A multiple of a number is obtained by multiplying it by other natural numbers. For example, multiples of 3 are 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, ... Prime numbers have exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Composite numbers have more than two factors.

sections.title: Introduction to Fractions
sections.content: A fraction represents a part of a whole. It is written as a/b where a is the numerator and b is the denominator (b ≠ 0). For example, 3/4 means 3 parts out of 4 equal parts. Proper fractions have numerator < denominator (e.g., 2/5). Improper fractions have numerator ≥ denominator (e.g., 7/4). Mixed fractions combine a whole number and a proper fraction (e.g., 1¾).

sections.title: Operations with Fractions
sections.content: To add or subtract fractions with the same denominator, add/subtract the numerators. For different denominators, find the LCM first. To multiply fractions, multiply numerators together and denominators together: a/b × c/d = ac/bd. To divide fractions, multiply by the reciprocal: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c = ad/bc.
